main_text.l: XIX. Hæc doctrina de distinctione na-
turæ ac subsistentiæ, ex Theologia descen-
dit, non ex Philosophia. Philosophus enim
sine ope Theologiæ vix ac ne vix quidem
agnoscere hanc, quam tradimus, differen-
tiam. Attamen in Theologia habet præ-
clarum usum, cum agitur de persona Chri-
sti θεανθρώπου [?], deque mysterio adorandæ
Trinitatis. Cur ergò ea de re agitur in
Metaphysicis, & non potius in Theolo-
gia? Ut intelligamus, illa Theologiæ do-
gmata, tametsi supra Philosophiam sint,
non tamen cum Philosophia pugnare. In
eum finem ita explicandæ sunt istæ Theo-
logorum voces, ut nulla in iis videatur ef-
se contradictio. Quod hæretici Trinitarii
perperam conantur ostendere.
CAP. III.
De distributione Entis in Deum &
Creaturam, & aliis æqui-
valentibus
THESIS I.
SOlet Ens in genere sumptum dividi
in Deum & Creaturam, sive in Ens à
Deo factum ac dependens: & quia hi
termini non satis noti sunt, vique suæ si-
gnificationis non ostendunt veritatem di-

page.notes: The Greek word after "Christi" (θεανθρώπου) is uncertain from the scan and is marked [?]. The word "ef-se" at the line end is the printed hyphenation of "esse" and is marked as uncertain. The large initial S of "Solet" is read as "SOlet" as printed. Long s has been normalised to s; the printed "s" forms in "subsistentiæ", "supra" and "sint" are plain s in the transcription.
